description: Does the agent reach for the right tool, and ONLY what the job needs? v2 replaces v1's denylist checks with allowlists, so a tool nobody predicted fails the case instead of slipping past.

cases.input: What is the weather in Singapore right now?
cases.rubric: Live external fact the model cannot know: one search, nothing else.

CurrentTimeInjector stamps the current time onto the last user message, so answering with no tool is correct and one datetime call is also correct. A web search or a second clock call is not. The reply must state the time the turn started, to within two minutes in the agent's timezone; a recording with no turn time cannot pass.

cases.input: How many days are there between 2024-02-14 and 2024-06-01?
cases.rubric: The injected clock answers 'now' and nothing else, so this span has to come from datetime's calculate action. Asserting the action too: tools_called_exactly sees only names, so a clock reading would otherwise score as correct date arithmetic.

cases.input: What is 17 times 3? Reply with just the number.
cases.rubric: Known-answer question: any tool call here is pure overhead, and a second model call means the first one failed to commit. v1 said this and could only forbid two tools by name.

cases.input: Remind me every weekday at 9am to check the deploy queue.
cases.rubric: A recurring reminder is a scheduled task, not a message the agent can promise to send later. The task_manager description instructs the model to call listRecurringTasks before creating one so duplicates do not accumulate, so the documented protocol is two calls and this case asserts that protocol rather than a bare minimum — an earlier version demanded one call and failed an agent that was following its tool's own instructions. The result assertion confirms a task was actually created; it deliberately does not pin the cron string, since '0 0 9 * * 1-5' and '0 0 9 * * MON-FRI' are the same schedule and substring matching cannot tell equivalent spellings apart.
The URL is already known — searching for it adds a round-trip and can land on a different page than the one asked for.
